summary: The guide said every other setting is in the database, but Start Lattice when Windows starts lives in the OS registration, the data folder's location in the bootstrap file, and the PDF Contents state in localStorage
harness_idea: Before a docs sentence says all others, list every place the app stores state (localStorage keys, bootstrap, OS registration, DB) and check each

summary: Each set_ui_prefs call waits for the store's lock on a task of its own, so two writes in flight could land the other way round and the library's older value would win at the next start
harness_idea: When several async commands write the same rows, send them through one queue and test the order with a stub that holds the first

summary: useSynced read the value in its first render and subscribed in an effect, so a start-up sync landing in between was missed until the screen was opened again
harness_idea: A hook that mirrors external state reads it again after subscribing (or uses useSyncExternalStore)

summary: The blocked-storage comment read as if the value were kept, though the modules read only the cache
The changelog said the first start copies this computer's settings, but a library that already has a row keeps the row and this computer's value is replaced
A key changed from A to B and back to A while the sync waits passes the snapshot check (ABA), so the row's value shows for that session
resolution: Needs two changes in the few milliseconds of the request; the next start shows A again

summary: Five of the seven settings could write localStorage alone and every test passed, though the library's older row would then win at the next start
harness_idea: A table test over SYNCED: each key changed from its screen reaches set_ui_prefs; a lint that every SYNCED key appears in it

summary: Only planSync's own test covered the snapshot rule; syncPrefs passing the first snapshot as the second passed every test
harness_idea: Test the wiring of a pure decision function through its caller with stubbed IO, not only the function

summary: The storage listener engines.ts gained had no test: cut, the URL bar would search with the cached engine for the session
Settings › Browser and Review following a storage event while open had no test
resolution: Same mechanism as Translation, which has one; it matters only when the sync lands while the screen is open

summary: Nothing tested that set_ui_prefs checks every key before writing any
resolution: The collect before the loop shows it; only the app's UI calls it, with the SYNCED keys
